shortDescription: Southern African company CPMZ's project to boost capacity of its pipeline between Mozambique and landlocked Zimbabwe by around two-thirds to cater for growing regional demand for diesel, petrol and jet fuel was officially launched on Wednesday.

children: Southern African company CPMZ's project to boost capacity of its pipeline between Mozambique and landlocked Zimbabwe by around two-thirds to cater for growing regional demand for diesel, petrol and jet fuel was officially launched on Wednesday.

The project will increase the annual capacity of the Beira-Harare pipeline connecting the port of Beira in Mozambique with the Feruka depot in Zimbabwe from 3 million cubic metres to 5 million cubic metres, company officials said.

The expansion, expected to be completed by the end of 2027, includes the construction of two pumping stations in the towns of Nhamatanda in central Mozambique and Messica, near the border with Zimbabwe, CPMZ said in a statement.
The statement said the presidents of Zimbabwe and Mozambique would attend the launch ceremony in Nhamatanda on Wednesday.
The project could be synchronised with a separate expansion of the Petrozim Line between Feruka, close to the border with Mozambique, and Zimbabwe's capital, Harare.

CPMZ said the 5 million cubic metres annual target is part of its goal to reach approximately 12 mcm a year through a larger diameter pipeline that would enable capacity to stay ahead of rising fuel demand. It is unclear when the larger diameter would be achieved.
